name: Josephine Bakhita
contribution: A Sudanese religious sister who joined the Canossians in 1896 after winning her freedom from slavery.

checks.lead: Josephine Margaret Bakhita,  (Arabic: جوزفين بخيتة; c. 1869 – 8 February 1947) was a Sudanese religious sister who joined the Canossians in 1896 after winning her freedom from slavery. She served in Italy for 50 years until her death in 1947. She was canonized in 2000, becoming the first female black saint in the modern era.
